additional_requirements: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

symptom.disease_info: Delusional Disorder is characterized by one or more fixed delusional beliefs, typically lasting at least one month, with overall functioning often more preserved than in schizophrenia and without the broader psychotic symptom pattern of schizophrenia. The course is often chronic and circumscribed, with people commonly presenting only after the belief causes interpersonal, occupational, legal, or medical friction despite contradictory evidence.

patient.stressor_event: Major change in the health or behavior of a family member
patient.stressor: When Thanh’s father developed a serious medical problem that required frequent appointments and lab monitoring, she took on a central role translating medical information and coordinating care for the family. During that year, her familiarity with clinic workflows and patient records fed a fixed belief that important health information was being deliberately altered or hidden, and reassurance from physicians, relatives, and colleagues did not change her conclusion. The belief increasingly dominated family conversations, volunteer health-fair interactions, and her efforts to pursue lab supervision, making her once-helpful precision feel adversarial to others. She ultimately sought psychiatric care herself after a community health mentor suggested that an independent mental health consultation might help her document and organize what had become an exhausting yearlong dispute.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: I’m here because for the past year I’ve been trying to prove that someone in the clinic system is changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results, and no matter how many doctors or family members tell me the numbers are fine, I know the chart doesn’t match what I saw and it’s wearing me down.

add_requirements.Functioning is not markedly impaired apa: Outside of the dispute about my dad’s records, I still keep my phlebotomy shifts, pay my bills, take care of myself, and manage normal day-to-day responsibilities.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: My family has started leaving me out of some appointment planning, and at work I feel like I’m no longer being considered for lab supervision because people think I make record issues too confrontational.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about a year, ever since my father’s medical problems started requiring frequent labs and appointments.
